The Agent reached this Judge only after submitting has_bug=true. Judge
defect_match by comparing the Agent final response and submitted
defect_description with the private Oracle.

Judge repair_match by directly comparing the submitted repair description,
modified_paths, deleted_paths, and modified file evidence with the Oracle
repair and corrected file evidence. The path sets must describe the same
complete repair, and the submitted files must have the same semantic effect as
the corrected files; textual identity is not required. If evidence is omitted
or insufficient to establish semantic equivalence, set repair_match to false.
If defect_match is false, repair_match must also be false.

```json
{
  "agent_answer": {
    "final_response": "Confirmed: `source/collator.py` is the only file with a modification timestamp from my session — the only file I changed. All other files (including all `data/*.jsonl`) remain untouched, as intended.

## Summary

**Defect found** in `source/collator.py`'s `PackedBatchCollator`. It packs `DOCUMENTS_PER_PACK=4` independent chat documents into one training sequence and correctly resets `position_ids` to 0 at each document boundary (and even computes `document_lengths`), but then builds `attention_mask = torch.ones_like(input_ids)` — a plain causal mask with **no document isolation**. `document_lengths` was otherwise unused anywhere in `source/`, confirming the isolation step was dropped.

I empirically confirmed the effect: with the same trailing document, changing an *earlier* packed document's content changed the later document's logits by up to ~9.9 (mean ~1.6) — real leakage, not noise. This meant ~75% of packed training tokens (every document after the first in a pack) were trained with attention to unrelated prior conversations, plus RoPE received nonsensical negative relative-position offsets across the reset boundaries — a mismatch versus the isolated, single-document evaluation path.

**Fix**: build a block-diagonal boolean causal mask from `document_lengths` so each document only attends to itself. Validated end-to-end (forward, backward, optimizer step) against the real model/adapter/data at stable scales; confirmed the leakage metric drops to near-zero residual (bf16 noise level) with the fix. Larger-scale runs hit intermittent CUDA "illegal instruction" errors in this sandbox, but I confirmed these reproduce identically with the pristine, unmodified original code — pre-existing GPU/driver flakiness in this session, unrelated to the fix.

```json
{
  "has_bug": true,
  "defect_description": "PackedBatchCollator (source/collator.py) packs DOCUMENTS_PER_PACK independent chat documents into one training sequence and resets position_ids to 0 per document, but builds attention_mask as torch.ones_like(input_ids) — a plain full causal mask with no per-document isolation. This lets later documents in a pack attend across unrelated earlier documents (confirmed empirically: changing an earlier packed document changes a later document's logits by up to ~9.9, mean ~1.6), and creates nonsensical negative RoPE relative-position offsets at pack boundaries. This corrupts the training signal for the majority of packed tokens and mismatches the isolated, per-document attention used at evaluation time. The collator also computes document_lengths but never uses it anywhere in source/, confirming the document-isolation step was implemented incompletely (metadata computed, but the mask that should consume it was never built).",
  "repair": {
    "description": "Modified PackedBatchCollator to build a block-diagonal causal attention mask from document_lengths, restricting each document's attention to its own tokens (still causal within itself), matching the position_ids reset and the isolated per-document behavior used during evaluation. Verified the mechanism (leakage eliminated to bf16 noise level) and end-to-end forward/backward/optimizer-step correctness against the real model, adapter, and training data.",
    "modified_paths": ["source/collator.py"]
  }
}
```",
    "submission": {
      "has_bug": true,
      "defect_description": "PackedBatchCollator (source/collator.py) packs DOCUMENTS_PER_PACK independent chat documents into one training sequence and resets position_ids to 0 per document, but builds attention_mask as torch.ones_like(input_ids) — a plain full causal mask with no per-document isolation. This lets later documents in a pack attend across unrelated earlier documents (confirmed empirically: changing an earlier packed document changes a later document's logits by up to ~9.9, mean ~1.6), and creates nonsensical negative RoPE relative-position offsets at pack boundaries. This corrupts the training signal for the majority of packed tokens and mismatches the isolated, per-document attention used at evaluation time. The collator also computes document_lengths but never uses it anywhere in source/, confirming the document-isolation step was implemented incompletely (metadata computed, but the mask that should consume it was never built).",
      "repair": {
        "description": "Modified PackedBatchCollator to build a block-diagonal causal attention mask from document_lengths, restricting each document's attention to its own tokens (still causal within itself), matching the position_ids reset and the isolated per-document behavior used during evaluation. Verified the mechanism (leakage eliminated to bf16 noise level) and end-to-end forward/backward/optimizer-step correctness against the real model, adapter, and training data.",
        "modified_paths": [
          "source/collator.py"
        ]
      }
    },
    "deleted_paths": [],
    "modified_files": "source/collator.py:
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import torch


class PackedBatchCollator:
    def __call__(self, rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if not rows:
            raise RuntimeError("cannot pack an empty document batch")
        input_ids = torch.tensor(
            [[
                token
                for row in rows
                for token in row["input_ids"]
            ]],
            dtype=torch.long,
        )
        position_ids = torch.tensor(
            [[
                position
                for row in rows
                for position in range(len(row["input_ids"]))
            ]],
            dtype=torch.long,
        )
        document_lengths = [len(row["input_ids"]) for row in rows]
        total_length = input_ids.shape[1]
        # Packed documents share one sequence but must stay mutually
        # invisible: each document's tokens may only attend to earlier
        # tokens within that same document, mirroring the isolated,
        # per-document attention that evaluation uses. Without this,
        # later documents in a pack silently attend into unrelated
        # earlier documents (and across nonsensical negative RoPE
        # offsets, since position_ids resets per document).
        segment_ids = torch.repeat_interleave(
            torch.arange(len(rows)),
            torch.tensor(document_lengths),
        )
        same_document = segment_ids.unsqueeze(0) == segment_ids.unsqueeze(1)
        causal = torch.tril(
            torch.ones(total_length, total_length, dtype=torch.bool)
        )
        attention_mask = (same_document & causal).view(
            1, 1, total_length, total_length
        )
        labels = input_ids.clone()
        return {
            "input_ids": input_ids,
            "attention_mask": attention_mask,
            "position_ids": position_ids,
            "labels": labels,
            "example_ids": [str(row["example_id"]) for row in rows],
            "document_lengths": document_lengths,
        }
"
  },
  "private_reference": {
    "oracle": {
      "has_bug": true,
      "defect_description": "Padding-free packing resets position IDs at each independent document, but the collator supplies a dense all-ones attention mask that permits cross-document attention and leaves every later document's first token active as a cross-document next-token target.",
      "repair": {
        "description": "Preserve the reset position IDs, omit the dense attention mask so the model derives independent packed segments, and set labels to -100 at every reset position so no document boundary creates a cross-document target.",
        "modified_paths": [
          "source/collator.py"
        ]
      }
    },
    "corrected_files": "source/collator.py:
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import torch


class PackedBatchCollator:
    def __call__(self, rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if not rows:
            raise RuntimeError("cannot pack an empty document batch")
        input_ids = torch.tensor(
            [[
                token
                for row in rows
                for token in row["input_ids"]
            ]],
            dtype=torch.long,
        )
        position_ids = torch.tensor(
            [[
                position
                for row in rows
                for position in range(len(row["input_ids"]))
            ]],
            dtype=torch.long,
        )
        labels = input_ids.clone()
        labels[position_ids == 0] = -100
        return {
            "input_ids": input_ids,
            "position_ids": position_ids,
            "labels": labels,
            "example_ids": [str(row["example_id"]) for row in rows],
            "document_lengths": [
                len(row["input_ids"]) for row in rows
            ],
        }
"
  }
}
